title: Practice Passage 9: When Clocks Changed the World

passage.title: When Clocks Changed the World
passage.sub_title: How the pursuit of precision timekeeping paved the way for modern navigation, commerce, and industrial society.
passage.content_html:
Paragraph A

[A1] Today, people rarely think about the importance of accurate timekeeping because clocks are found almost everywhere. [A2] Mobile phones, computers, watches, and even kitchen appliances display the time automatically. [A3] However, for most of human history, measuring time precisely was extremely difficult. [A4] Communities relied mainly on the position of the Sun, the movement of stars, or simple devices such as sundials and water clocks.

Paragraph B

[B1] Early methods of timekeeping worked reasonably well under certain conditions. [B2] Sundials were useful during sunny weather but became useless at night or on cloudy days. [B3] Water clocks measured time by allowing water to flow slowly between containers, although the flow could change with temperature or damage to the equipment. [B4] These limitations encouraged inventors to search for more dependable methods.

Paragraph C

[C1] During the Middle Ages, mechanical clocks appeared in parts of Europe. [C2] Unlike earlier devices, these clocks used gears and weights to produce regular movement. [C3] Although they were not perfectly accurate, they represented an important technological improvement. [C4] Many of the first mechanical clocks were installed in church towers so that entire communities could hear the bells marking each hour.

Paragraph D

[D1] The demand for greater accuracy increased as international trade expanded. [D2] Merchants needed reliable schedules for transporting goods over long distances. [D3] Sailors also depended on accurate clocks because navigation at sea required precise measurements of time. [D4] Improvements in clockmaking therefore supported both commerce and exploration.

Paragraph E

[E1] The Industrial Revolution created new reasons for accurate timekeeping. [E2] Factories required workers to begin and finish shifts at fixed times. [E3] Railway companies also needed standard timetables to reduce confusion and improve safety. [E4] Before national railway schedules existed, neighbouring towns sometimes used slightly different local times, making travel more complicated.

Paragraph F

[F1] Modern technology has transformed timekeeping once again. [F2] Atomic clocks measure time using the natural behaviour of atoms and are far more accurate than traditional mechanical clocks. [F3] Their precision supports satellite navigation, international communications, and scientific research. [F4] Although most people never see an atomic clock, they benefit from its accuracy every day.

Paragraph G

[G1] Historians argue that clocks have influenced society in ways that extend beyond technology. [G2] They changed how businesses operate, how transport systems are organised, and how individuals plan their daily routines. [G3] Rather than simply measuring time, clocks gradually changed the relationship between people and time itself. [G4] Their history demonstrates how a single invention can influence many different aspects of civilisation.
